```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tang_2026_zidovudine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tang_2026_zidovudine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-49905-1> (open access)

Tang 2026 links plasma zidovudine (AZT) to its intracellular
phosphorylated anabolites in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs).
Plasma AZT is taken up into the cell, effluxes back, and is phosphorylated
stepwise and reversibly to the mono-, di- and triphosphate (AZT-MP, AZT-DP
and AZT-TP; Figure 1 of the paper). All transfers are first order. The
authors fitted this intracellular layer to each volunteer's PBMC data in
ADAPT II, using that volunteer's observed plasma AZT profile as the input
function. They say plasma AZT follows a two-compartment model but print
none of its parameters. The packaged model therefore takes plasma AZT as
the time-varying covariate `CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM` (umol/L) and has no dosing
compartment.

# Population

Six healthy Chinese adult volunteers took part: two men and four women,
aged 22-26 years, weighing 49-80 kg and 158-180 cm tall (Methods
"Volunteer recruitment" and the opening of the clinical Results). Each
received one 600 mg oral dose of zidovudine after an overnight fast.
Plasma and PBMC samples were taken before dosing and at 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2,
2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 h. AZT, AZT-MP, AZT-DP and AZT-TP were
quantified in PBMCs by HPLC-MS/MS and are reported in ng per 10^6 cells.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tang_2026_zidovudine")()$population`.

# Source trace

Each value's origin is also recorded as an in-file comment beside its
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Tang_2026_zidovudine.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lkinf_pbmc` (paper `kin`) | 1.22 ng/10^6 cells/uM/h | Table 2 |
| `lkeff_pbmc` (paper `kout`) | 3.76 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lkmet_zdvmp` (paper `kO-MP`) | 0.478 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lkicv` (paper `kMP-O`) | 0.792 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lkmet_zdvdp` (paper `kMP-DP`) | 0.659 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lkicv_zdvmp` (paper `kDP-MP`) | 1.72 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lkmet_zdvtp` (paper `kDP-TP`) | 3.18 1/h | Table 2 |
| `lkicv_zdvdp` (paper `kTP-DP`) | 4.62 1/h | Table 2 |
| `eta` variances | `log(1 + CV^2)` with CV 39, 72, 45, 62, 81, 76, 79, 88 % | Table 2 `%CV` column |
| `propSd_*` | `fixed(0)` | not reported (see Assumptions) |
| `d/dt(pbmc)` | uptake `kin * Cp`, loss `(kout + kO-MP)`, return `kMP-O * MP` | Figure 1; Eqs. 1-2 (transport and first phosphorylation) |
| `d/dt(pbmc_zdvmp)`, `d/dt(pbmc_zdvdp)`, `d/dt(pbmc_zdvtp)` | reversible first-order chain | Figure 1; Methods "Transportation and phosphorylation pathway model" |
| Plasma input `CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM` | umol/L | units of `kin` in Table 2; Eqs. 1-3 |

# Plasma input function

The packaged model needs a plasma AZT profile. The paper's own input
functions were each volunteer's observed plasma data, which are not
published individually. The maintainers digitised the mean profile of
Figure 4 (marker centres, calibrated on the axis labels) and convert it
from ng/mL to umol/L with the zidovudine molecular weight 267.2 g/mol.

```{r plasma-input}
mw_zdv <- 267.2 # g/mol, as used by Fauchet_2013_zidovudine
plasma <- tibble::tibble(
  time = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10),
  cp_ngml = c(0, 3003, 2793, 2143, 1478, 1045, 777, 705, 474, 358, 207, 98, 55)
) |>
  mutate(CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM = cp_ngml / mw_zdv)

ggplot(plasma, aes(time, cp_ngml)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma AZT (ng/mL)",
    title = "Figure 4 - mean plasma AZT after 600 mg orally (digitised)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Tang 2026 (digitised mean; the input function for every simulation below)."
  )
```

```{r event-helper}
# One observation row every 0.05 h over the paper's 0-10 h sampling window.
# CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM is interpolated linearly between the digitised samples.
# The model has four declared endpoints and no dose, so every observation row
# carries a real ODE state as cmt plus dvid = 1L.
grid <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.05)
make_events <- function(n, id_offset = 0L) {
  one <- tibble::tibble(
    time = grid,
    evid = 0L,
    amt = NA_real_,
    cmt = "pbmc",
    dvid = 1L,
    CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM = approx(plasma$time, plasma$CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM, grid)$y
  )
  tidyr::crossing(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), one) |>
    arrange(id, time)
}
```

# Simulation

## Typical value

```{r simulate-typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Tang_2026_zidovudine")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "omega")

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_typical,
  events = make_events(1L),
  covsInterpolation = "linear",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

analyte_cols <- c(
  "AZT" = "Cpbmc", "AZT-MP" = "Cpbmc_zdvmp",
  "AZT-DP" = "Cpbmc_zdvdp", "AZT-TP" = "Cpbmc_zdvtp"
)
typ_long <- sim_typ |>
  select(time, all_of(analyte_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, levels = names(analyte_cols)))
```

## Between-subject variability

Two hundred virtual subjects share the mean plasma input; only the eight
intracellular rate constants vary, with the Table 2 coefficients of
variation.

```{r simulate-vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260424)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = make_events(200L),
  covsInterpolation = "linear",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
vpc_long <- sim_vpc |>
  select(id, time, all_of(analyte_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(-id, -time), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, levels = names(analyte_cols)))
```

# Replicate published figures

The mean PBMC profiles of Figure 5 were digitised by the maintainers from
the published figure (marker centres calibrated on the axis labels; the
AZT-MP peak at 1.5 h was read from an enlarged crop because its error bar
merges with the marker).

```{r figure-5}
obs_fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~AZT,    ~`AZT-MP`, ~`AZT-DP`, ~`AZT-TP`,
  0.5,   0.105,   0.172,     0.0399,    0.0244,
  1,     0.133,   0.313,     0.0647,    0.0244,
  1.5,   0.118,   0.876,     0.0754,    0.0638,
  2,     0.0843,  0.453,     0.0501,    0.0558,
  2.5,   0.0501,  0.321,     0.0357,    0.0377,
  3,     0.0354,  0.214,     0.0336,    0.0295,
  3.5,   0.0305,  0.197,     0.0376,    0.0310,
  4,     0.0256,  0.169,     0.0334,    0.0238,
  5,     0.0203,  0.174,     0.0353,    0.0201,
  6,     0.0196,  0.164,     0.0258,    0.0185,
  8,     0.0098,  0.152,     0.0223,    0.0144,
  10,    0.0060,  0.162,     0.0237,    0.0102
) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = factor(analyte, levels = names(analyte_cols)))

vpc_summary <- vpc_long |>
  group_by(analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05),
    q50 = quantile(conc, 0.50),
    q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = vpc_summary, aes(time, ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = vpc_summary, aes(time, q50), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = typ_long, aes(time, conc), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = obs_fig5, aes(time, conc), colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "PBMC concentration (ng/10^6 cells)",
    title = "Figure 5 - PBMC AZT and anabolites after 600 mg orally",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 5 of Tang 2026. Red points: digitised observed means.",
      "Blue: typical-value prediction. Dashed line and band: median and 90% interval of 200 virtual subjects."
    )
  )
```

Only AZT-MP is close to the observed means. Its typical-value peak
height and its 10 h level agree to within about 5%, but the predicted
peak is broader: it stays near 0.7-0.9 ng/10^6 cells from 1.5 to 4 h,
while the observed mean falls back to about 0.2 by 3 h. Intracellular AZT
is over-predicted about 17-fold at its 1 h peak. AZT-DP and AZT-TP are
over-predicted about 3- to 4-fold at their peaks, and their predicted
peaks come about 2 h later than observed. The section on deviations
below discusses this mismatch.

```{r figure-5-checks}
typ_at <- function(col, t) sim_typ[[col]][which.min(abs(sim_typ$time - t))]
obs_at <- function(a, t) obs_fig5$conc[obs_fig5$analyte == a & obs_fig5$time == t]

mp_peak_ratio <- max(sim_typ$Cpbmc_zdvmp) / 0.922 # Table 1 AZT-MP Cmax
mp_10h_ratio <- typ_at("Cpbmc_zdvmp", 10) / obs_at("AZT-MP", 10)
azt_peak_ratio <- max(sim_typ$Cpbmc) / 0.175 # Table 1 AZT Cmax

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Check = c(
      "AZT-MP peak, typical / Table 1 Cmax",
      "AZT-MP at 10 h, typical / Figure 5 mean",
      "AZT peak, typical / Table 1 Cmax"
    ),
    Ratio = signif(c(mp_peak_ratio, mp_10h_ratio, azt_peak_ratio), 3)
  ),
  caption = "Typical-value predictions against the published means."
)

stopifnot(
  # The typical-value solve uses no random draws, so these ratios are
  # deterministic (measured 1.01 and 0.96). A mis-transcribed rate constant
  # in the MP formation / loss balance moves them by tens of percent.
  abs(log(mp_peak_ratio)) < log(1.25),
  abs(log(mp_10h_ratio)) < log(1.25)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Table 1 of the paper gives the non-compartmental parameters of the four
PBMC species (mean of the six volunteers). The simulated cohort is
analysed the same way, one PKNCA analysis per analyte over the 0-10 h
sampling window. There is no dose in this model (plasma is the input), so
no dose object is passed.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- vpc_long |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  # LSODA can undershoot zero by ~atol in the first step; floor it.
  mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0)) |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10)) |>
  mutate(analyte = as.character(analyte))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | analyte + id)
# AUC0-t, Cmax and Tmax over the 0-10 h sampling window as in Table 1;
# AUC0-inf and the terminal half-life extrapolated from the same samples.
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0),
  end = c(10, Inf),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  tmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
# Some virtual subjects' AZT-DP / AZT-TP profiles are still near their peak
# at 10 h, leaving fewer than three post-peak points; PKNCA then warns and
# returns NA for that half-life. Muffle only that warning and count the NAs.
nca_res <- withCallingHandlers(
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, intervals = intervals)),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("Too few points for half-life", conditionMessage(w))) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
)
hl_missing <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  group_by(analyte) |>
  summarise(n_missing = sum(is.na(PPORRES)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(
  hl_missing,
  caption = "Virtual subjects (of 200) without a terminal half-life over 0-10 h."
)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

```{r nca-compare}
# Tang 2026 Table 1 (means of the six volunteers; AUC0-t is over 0-10 h).
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~analyte, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "AZT",    0.175, 1.083, 0.371,    0.396,       2.493,
  "AZT-MP", 0.922, 1.500, 2.548,    6.343,       13.428,
  "AZT-DP", 0.076, 1.417, 0.345,    0.615,       8.285,
  "AZT-TP", 0.062, 1.583, 0.223,    0.279,       4.240
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "analyte",
  units = c(
    cmax = "ng/10^6 cells", tmax = "h", auclast = "ng*h/10^6 cells",
    aucinf.obs = "ng*h/10^6 cells", half.life = "h"
  ),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (median of 200 virtual subjects) vs. Tang 2026 Table 1 (mean of 6). * differs from reference by >20%."
)
```

The comparison mirrors the figure. AZT-MP Cmax and AUC0-inf agree with
Table 1 to within about 5%, but the broader simulated peak makes AUC0-10
about 1.9-fold the published value. Intracellular AZT is about 17-fold
higher than published in Cmax and about 25-fold higher in AUC. AZT-DP
and AZT-TP are 3- to 5-fold higher, with Tmax about 2 h later. The published terminal half-lives (13.4 h for
AZT-MP, 8.3 h for AZT-DP) come from profiles that are still flat at 10 h,
whereas the model, with efflux of parent AZT as the only exit, gives a
common terminal phase. Half-lives fitted over a 10 h window are therefore
not well determined on either side.

# Steady state under constant exposure

The paper's in-vitro experiments (Figures 2 and 3) held the medium
concentration constant. The model then has a closed-form steady state:
every phosphorylation step is reversible and efflux of parent AZT is the
only exit, so each pair of forward and backward fluxes balances.
`AZT = kin * Cp / kout`, `MP = AZT * kO-MP / kMP-O`,
`DP = MP * kMP-DP / kDP-MP` and `TP = DP * kDP-TP / kTP-DP`. A long
constant-input solve has to reach these values.

```{r steady-state}
cp_const <- 100 # umol/L, the Figure 3 medium concentration
ev_ss <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1L, time = c(0, 50, 100), evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_,
  cmt = "pbmc", dvid = 1L, CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM = cp_const
)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical,
  events = ev_ss, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
theta <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta
p <- exp(theta[c(
  "lkinf_pbmc", "lkeff_pbmc", "lkmet_zdvmp", "lkicv",
  "lkmet_zdvdp", "lkicv_zdvmp", "lkmet_zdvtp", "lkicv_zdvdp"
)])
azt_ss <- p[["lkinf_pbmc"]] * cp_const / p[["lkeff_pbmc"]]
mp_ss <- azt_ss * p[["lkmet_zdvmp"]] / p[["lkicv"]]
dp_ss <- mp_ss * p[["lkmet_zdvdp"]] / p[["lkicv_zdvmp"]]
tp_ss <- dp_ss * p[["lkmet_zdvtp"]] / p[["lkicv_zdvdp"]]
closed <- c(azt_ss, mp_ss, dp_ss, tp_ss)
solved <- unlist(sim_ss[sim_ss$time == 100, unname(analyte_cols)])

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Analyte = names(analyte_cols),
    `Closed form (ng/10^6 cells)` = signif(closed, 4),
    `Solved at 100 h` = signif(solved, 4)
  ),
  caption = "Steady state at a constant 100 umol/L plasma (medium) concentration."
)
# Same parameters on both sides, so the difference is integrator error only
# (measured ~1e-9 at rtol 1e-10).
stopifnot(max(abs(solved / closed - 1)) < 1e-6)
```

These steady-state levels are the same order of magnitude as the plateaus
in Figure 3, where intracellular AZT reached about 20-30 ng/10^6 cells in
Molt-4 cells and 70-80 in HUVECs, and AZT-MP about 40-60 and 100-130. The
model, fitted to PBMCs, predicts 32 and 20. The in-vitro data were not
used to fit the model and are shown for context only.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **No plasma PK layer.** The paper describes plasma AZT with a
  two-compartment model but prints none of its parameters (only the NCA
  Tmax of 0.62 +/- 0.20 h and half-life of 1.95 +/- 0.20 h). The
  intracellular layer was fitted with each volunteer's observed plasma
  data as the input function, so the packaged model takes plasma AZT as
  the covariate `CP_ZIDOVUDINE_UM` and users supply the trajectory. This
  vignette uses the digitised mean of Figure 4. The paediatric
  `Fauchet_2013_zidovudine` model is the only zidovudine plasma model in
  nlmixr2lib; its `Cc` (mg/L) divided by 0.2672 gives umol/L.
- **Units of the plasma input.** Table 2 gives `kin` in ng/10^6 cells per
  uM per h, so the input is in umol/L. The MW of 267.2 g/mol used to
  convert the digitised ng/mL profile is the value `Fauchet_2013_zidovudine`
  uses; Tang 2026 does not state one.
- **Mass, not molar, intracellular amounts.** Each PBMC species is carried
  in ng/10^6 cells, the unit in which Table 1 and Figure 5 report it, and
  the first-order constants act on those amounts directly. That is
  presumably how the ADAPT fit was set up, but the paper does not say.
  Because the four species have different molecular weights (267, 347,
  427 and 507 g/mol), a mass-based chain does not conserve moles.
- **Reversible steps from Figure 1.** Eq. 2 writes the AZT balance without
  the AZT-MP -> AZT return term. The model follows Figure 1 and Table 2,
  which give a backward rate constant for every phosphorylation step.
- **IIV from %CV.** Table 2 reports the mean and %CV of the six individual
  MAP-Bayesian estimates. The %CV was converted to a log-normal variance,
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, with no correlations because none are
  reported.
- **Residual error.** The text before Table 2 says the table presents
  residual error variances, but none is printed and the ADAPT variance
  model is not described. All four proportional residual SDs are
  `fixed(0)`, so simulations are of the true intracellular concentration.
- **Typical values are means of individual estimates.** With six subjects
  and CVs of 39-88%, the arithmetic mean of each rate constant need not
  reproduce the mean profile.
- **Mismatch with the published means.** With the Table 2 means and the
  Figure 4 mean plasma profile as input, only the AZT-MP peak height, 10 h
  level and AUC0-inf are reproduced, and its peak is too broad (AUC0-10
  about 1.9-fold). Intracellular AZT is over-predicted about 17-fold at
  Cmax and 25-fold in AUC, and AZT-DP and AZT-TP 3- to 5-fold. The maintainers checked whether a different unit for the plasma
  input could explain this: reading `kin` per (ug/mL) instead of per uM
  shrinks the AZT miss to about 6-fold but makes AZT-MP 3.5-fold too low,
  so the uM reading printed in Table 2 is retained. The values were not
  tuned. The model ratio `kin / kout` (0.32 ng/10^6 cells per uM) agrees
  with the in-vitro plateaus (about 0.2-0.8), which suggests the clinical
  PBMC AZT data, not the transport constants, sit apart. The source of the
  discrepancy could not be identified from the paper.
- **In-vitro medium concentration.** The Methods give 50 uM for the
  time-course experiment, while the Results and the Figure 3 caption give
  100 uM. The steady-state check above uses 100 uM; it is a property of
  the model and does not depend on this choice.
- **No corrections.** No erratum or correction notice was found for the
  article as of 2026-11-13. It has no supplementary material, and its data
  availability statement says all data are in the published article.
